cells.A3: Purpose. This workbook helps Aurj find the creators, communities, institutions, and media channels that already reach our target learners (Urdu- and Hindi-speaking youth in Pakistan, India, and the diaspora). It tracks audience fit and relationships that can lead to guest features, co-created content, workshops, and cross-promotion. It is an audience-access system, not a list of people to pay.
cells.A4: Use it when: you are researching new prospects, planning weekly outreach, or deciding who to focus on next.
cells.A7: 1. On the Prospects sheet, delete row 2 (marked [EXAMPLE]) and the example row on the Interaction Log once you understand how they work.
cells.A8: 2. Open Target Map. It sets how many of the 100 slots each category should have. Start with the largest categories: Urdu career YouTubers, Pakistan-focused freelancing educators, and student communities.
cells.A9: 3. Research before scoring. Read 10 recent posts or videos, look at comment quality, and find a public business contact method. Record only what you can verify.
cells.A10: 4. Score the four 1-5 fields (Audience Relevance, Engagement Quality, Accessibility, Collaboration Potential) using the rubric on Scoring Guide.
cells.A11: 5. Set Relationship Status, Next Action, and Follow-up Date. Priority Score and Priority Tier calculate automatically.
cells.A12: 6. Log every touchpoint on Interaction Log, then update Last Interaction on the prospect's row.
cells.A13: 7. Review the Dashboard weekly: overdue follow-ups, tier counts, and category gaps.
cells.A17: •  Prospects: main database with 150 rows and columns A to X. Grey columns V and W are formulas. Do not type over them.
cells.A18: •  Interaction Log: one row per touchpoint (up to 300). Prospect Name fills in automatically from the ID.
cells.A19: •  Scoring Guide: editable weights and tier thresholds (blue cells), plus the 1-5 rubric for each field.
cells.A20: •  Target Map: category targets (total 100) and where to look for each category. Edit the blue numbers; the Dashboard recalculates gaps.
cells.A21: •  Lists: dropdown sources. Keep the category names identical to Target Map.
cells.A24: •  ID: unique code (P001 to P150). Used by the Interaction Log. Do not change.
cells.A25: •  Name / Organization / Channel: the name the person uses publicly, and the brand, show, publication, or community name.
cells.A26: •  Category: choose from the list in Target Map.
cells.A27: •  Audience Language and Audience Region: where most of their audience actually is, based on what you can see (comments, language of content, location cues). Verify rather than assume.
cells.A28: •  Why Relevant to Aurj: one or two sentences tied to an Aurj pillar (English/Communication, Business/Money, UI/UX/Design, Discipline/Mindset) or a mission topic.
cells.A29: •  Primary Platform, Primary Profile URL, Primary Audience Size: largest platform, public URL, and current follower or subscriber count entered as a number. Follower count is for reference only and never affects the score.
cells.A30: •  Secondary Platform: second platform where they are active. Paste its URL into Notes.
cells.A31: •  Audience Relevance, Engagement Quality, Accessibility, Collaboration Potential: scored 1-5 using Scoring Guide. Relevance carries the most weight and gates Tier A.
cells.A32: •  Best Opportunity Type: the format most likely to work with them first (guest, co-created content, workshop, and so on).
cells.A33: •  Contact Email / Page: public business email, contact page, or booking link only.
cells.A34: •  Relationship Status: stage in the relationship (see below).
cells.A35: •  Last Interaction / Next Action / Follow-up Date: date of the last touchpoint, the specific next step, and when to act. Overdue dates turn red; dates due within 7 days turn amber.
cells.A36: •  Priority Score (auto): 0-100 weighted score from the four 1-5 fields.
cells.A37: •  Priority Tier (auto): A (pursue now), B (build relationship), C (monitor). Not a Fit becomes Archived.
cells.A38: •  Notes: competitive overlap, recent posts, pitch angles, and any secondary URL.
cells.A41: Not Contacted, Researching, Following, Engaging, Connected, In Conversation, Collaboration Proposed, Collaborating. Choose Not a Fit at any stage to archive a prospect. Priority scoring then stops and the prospect is excluded from follow-up alerts.
cells.A44: •  Contact only through public business channels or open invitations. Do not message people through private groups without permission. Do not collect personal phone numbers or private information.
cells.A45: •  Skill-training institutes: zero paid promotion. Monetization happens only through honest, disclosed channels.
cells.A46: •  Record only what is publicly visible or what the person has said directly. Do not record assumptions about someone's personal life, health, religion, or finances.
cells.A47: •  Check follower counts and audience details yourself before scoring. Do not copy unverified numbers.
cells.A50: •  Daily, about 20 minutes: research 3 to 5 new prospects and log 3 to 5 touchpoints.
cells.A51: •  Monday: clear the overdue follow-ups on the Dashboard.
cells.A52: •  Friday: review tiers, move stalled prospects to Not a Fit, and adjust Target Map if a category is over- or under-performing.
cells.A54: Colour key: blue text = editable input or setting. Grey fill = automatic formula (do not overwrite). Grey italic example rows = delete before use.

cells.A2: Everything on this sheet calculates automatically from the Prospects and Interaction Log sheets.

cells.D22: No public contact. Access only through third parties.
cells.E22: Unlikely, or conflicts with Aurj's values (for example, a paid-promotion-only offer).
cells.A24: How Audience Relevance is judged: look at who comments, their language, their country, and whether topics match Aurj's pillars and mission. Follower count is recorded for reference but does not affect any score.

cells.A1: Target Map: where the 100 prospects should come from
cells.A2: Targets are starting points, not fixed quotas. Edit column B; the Dashboard shows the gap to each target. Total must stay at 100.
cells.C5: Our core audience already watches Urdu-language career, skills, and money content. These creators are the closest match to Aurj's language and mission.
cells.D5: Search YouTube in Urdu for freelancing, skills, career, and money topics. Check which channels get Urdu comments from students. Review related channels shown beside our own videos.
cells.E5: Guest appearance, live workshop, co-created video
cells.F5: Rank creators higher when comments show students asking for next steps, not just views.
cells.C6: Freelancing is one of Aurj's core skills. Creators who teach Pakistani youth to earn online already hold the audience we want.
cells.D6: Search freelancing tutorials that mention Pakistan or Pakistani students. Check Pakistani freelancing groups and channels. Note who speaks at local freelancing meetups.
cells.F6: Some of these creators sell courses. Note competitive overlap and position Aurj as complementary.
cells.C7: Long-form listeners are often students and early-career professionals who give time to learning.
cells.D7: Browse Spotify and Apple Podcasts for Urdu and Hindi education, career, and business shows. Filter by language.
cells.F7: Audio-first audiences respond to founder stories. Pitch a specific episode topic, not a general interview.
cells.C8: Campus societies, student councils, and large youth WhatsApp or Discord communities give direct access to students. Admins often share useful resources.
cells.D8: University society pages on Instagram and Facebook, campus event listings, LinkedIn student-body pages, admins of active public communities.
cells.E8: Campus talk or event, ambassador program, community share
cells.F8: Verify size and activity before outreach. Never add people to groups without their consent.
cells.C9: Technical and vocational institutes (NAVTTC, TEVTA, PSDF-linked and private institutes) reach students Aurj wants to serve. Relationships support the planned honest awareness series.
cells.D9: Official government portals and public institute pages. Campus event calendars and public announcements.
cells.F9: Strict rule: zero paid promotion from institutes. Monetization only through honest channels. Log every interaction.
cells.C10: Pakistan-focused tech newsletters, blogs, and publications reach founders and early-career people who are part of Aurj's older audience.
cells.D10: Pakistani tech news sites, newsletter directories, bylines of recent Pakistani startup coverage.
cells.F10: Pitch stories (for example, OIT's face-to-face teaching in Khushab) rather than product features.
cells.C11: Incubators, accelerators, and founder creators reach ambitious youth who want to start companies and raise funds, both Aurj mission topics.
cells.D11: Public incubator and accelerator alumni pages, founder podcasts, LinkedIn founder posts from Pakistan.
cells.F11: Judge relevance by how often they work with early-stage founders, not by funding announcements.
cells.C12: This matches Aurj's English/Communication pillar (Waqar Shah Sir). Spoken and written English is a gateway skill for jobs and freelancing.
cells.D12: YouTube searches for spoken English, interview English, and communication skills in Urdu. LinkedIn communication coaches from Pakistan and India.
cells.F12: Many teach in Urdu. Check that their teaching style fits Aurj's voice before pitching.
cells.C13: This matches Aurj's UI/UX/Design pillar (Mustafa). Design learners are a high-intent audience for freelancing.
cells.D13: YouTube and portfolio-focused creators teaching design in Urdu or English. Figma community educators.
cells.F13: Confirm they reach South Asian learners, not only global audiences.
cells.C14: Students finishing matric, FSc, and entrance tests are a large youth audience. Overlap with Aurj is in study discipline and career planning.
cells.D14: YouTube searches for matric, FSc, and entry-test prep channels. School and college prep Facebook pages.
cells.E14: Cross-promotion, guest session on discipline or career planning
cells.F14: Keep outreach aligned with the Discipline/Mindset pillar (Tabish). Avoid implying exam-passing guarantees.
cells.C15: This matches Aurj's Discipline/Mindset pillar. Motivational audiences are large, but relevance depends on whether they move into skill-building.
cells.D15: Urdu motivation and productivity channels. TikTok and Instagram Reels creators with Urdu captions.
cells.F15: High reach can mean low fit. Score carefully on Audience Relevance and Engagement Quality.
cells.C16: Hindi-speaking learners in India and the diaspora (UK, Gulf, North America) are part of Aurj's stated audience. These creators reach them in their language.
cells.D16: YouTube and Instagram Hindi career and skills creators. Diaspora student communities.
cells.F16: Confirm audience geography. Do not assume a Pakistan audience just because the language matches.
cells.C17: Peer platforms serving similar learners can cross-promote without being direct competitors. Their public content can also reveal what Aurj's audience already uses.
cells.D17: Public posts from ed-tech founders, learning-platform newsletters, Urdu and Hindi education startups.
cells.F17: Partner only where both sides serve learners. Record competitive notes in the Notes column.
